video_caption: The black and white video segment opens with two men in traditional judo gis bowing to each other on a mat, with several other men also in judo gis kneeling respectfully in the background. They then begin a demonstration, with one man executing a powerful shoulder throw (likely seoi nage) on the other, who is lifted and thrown to the mat. After resetting, the same man performs another, even higher and more dynamic shoulder throw, lifting his partner completely into the air before slamming him down. The video then transitions to a dark gray screen with white Japanese text, which reads: "消えた技" (Kieta Waza), meaning "Lost Techniques," followed by "忘れられた技法" (Wasure rareta Gihō), meaning "Forgotten Techniques." This text suggests the demonstration showcases historical or seldom-seen judo techniques.

The video displays a historical, black and white photograph from 1928, showing two men in martial arts gis demonstrating a judo technique. The man on the left, wearing a white gi with a dark belt, is shorter and appears to be executing the throw (tori). He has his left arm wrapped around the waist of the taller man on the right, who is wearing a dark gi, gripping his belt, while his right hand holds the opponent's left sleeve near the shoulder. The taller man (uke) has his right arm around the tori's neck/shoulder area. This specific grip is being demonstrated as a setup for a Seoi Otoshi (shoulder drop throw), characterized by hooking the arm like a shoulder throw but also reaching around the waist to grab the opponent's belt. The background features a simple, possibly wooden, wall and a textured floor. Japanese text at the bottom provides context: "口絵1: 背負落" (Kōe 1: Seoi Otoshi - Frontispiece 1: Shoulder Drop) and "南郷正毅西段「柔道正解」昭和3年" (Nango Masanori Nishidan "Judo Seikai" Showa 3 nen - Nango Masanori 6th Dan "Judo Seikai" Showa 3 (1928)).

The video demonstrates the judo technique "Seoi-otoshi" with two men dressed in white judo gis. The man wearing a black belt (Tori) executes the throw, while the man wearing a red belt (Uke) is thrown. The scene is set in a dojo with a light blue wall in the background and a light-colored judo mat on the floor. The Kodokan logo is visible in the top-left corner, and the IJF Academy logo is in the top-right corner. The throw begins with both men gripping each other's gi, then Tori pivots, drops to one or both knees, and pulls Uke over his back, causing Uke to fall to the mat. The video cycles through several repetitions of the throw from different angles, highlighting the movement from various perspectives, with the text "Seoi-otoshi" consistently displayed at the bottom left of the screen, identifying the technique.

The video opens with a black and white line drawing depicting a judo throw. One martial artist (Uke) is being thrown over the back of another (Tori), whose body is low to the ground, suggesting a sacrifice throw. Uke is mid-air, legs elevated. Below the drawing, Japanese text reads: "写真6 釣落" (Shashin 6 Tsuri Otoshi), which translates to "Photo 6 Tsuri Otoshi" (a judo throw). The second line reads: "有馬純臣 四段「通俗柔道図解」明治38年" (Arima Sumiyuki Yodan "Tsūzoku Jūdō Zukai" Meiji 38 nen), translating to "Sumiyuki Arima 4th Dan 'Illustrated Popular Judo' Meiji 38th year" (referring to 1905). At the 0:55 mark, the scene transitions to a black and white video of two individuals in white judo gis demonstrating a throw on a light-colored mat against a dark background. The person wearing a black belt (Tori) grips the white-belted opponent (Uke). Tori pulls Uke forward, drops to one knee, and executes a throw that sends Uke over Tori's hip and back, landing Uke on the mat head-first before rolling onto their back. The video then replays the sequence in reverse, and then plays the throw once more from the beginning.

The video segment displays a static black and white illustration of two figures, likely martial artists, dressed in traditional gis. One figure (Uke) is bent over, leaning forward, while the other (Tori) is behind them, applying a throw or sweep. Tori's left foot is positioned against Uke's right foot at the ankle, while Tori's arms are gripping Uke's upper body, appearing to pull them sideways. A small, indistinct Japanese text "(分 大)" is visible within the drawing itself. Below the image, there is Japanese text that reads: "写真11 大横分" (Photo 11: Large Yoko-wakare/Side Separation) and "『日本百科大辞典』 明治43年" (Nihon Hyakka Daijiten [Japan Encyclopedia]: Meiji 43rd year), indicating the illustration is from a 1910 Japanese encyclopedia.

The video showcases different examples of a specific judo throw, beginning with two female judokas on a yellow competition mat with a white Suzuki banner in the background. The judoka in the blue gi grapples with her opponent in the white gi, then pulls her to the side and executes a successful throw, landing her opponent on her side. This action is repeated from a slightly different angle. The scene then transitions to older competition footage, where two female judokas, both in white gis (one with a red belt, the other a black belt), perform a similar throw. The red-belted judoka grabs her opponent's leg, lifts her, flattens herself, and throws the opponent sideways. The video concludes with a black and white historical photograph showing two men in judogi grappling, accompanied by Japanese text: "写真 8 横分 徳見十一段 [柔道手引] 明治42年" (Photo 8: Yoko-wake Tokumi 11th dan [Judo Tehik] Meiji 42nd year), providing a historical reference to the techniques being discussed.

The video segment begins with two men in white judo gis and black belts facing each other on a grey mat against a light blue background. One man wears a white undershirt beneath his gi. The text "Nage-no-kata" (Throwing Forms) appears briefly at the top right. They demonstrate a judo throw, where the man on the left (Tori) pulls and sweeps the leg of the man on the right (Uke), causing Uke to fall backward onto the mat. A close-up then shows bare feet on the mat, with one foot lifting its heel and then pressing down firmly. This is followed by an extreme close-up of a hand gripping a gi sleeve. The scene returns to the two men, who repeatedly demonstrate different variations of throws. In one instance, Tori steps in and executes a throw, pulling Uke forward and over his hip, causing Uke to fall flat on his back. In another, Tori sweeps Uke's leg and pulls him sideways to the mat. The throws involve precise footwork, gripping, and body rotation, emphasizing the technique of off-balancing and redirecting an opponent's weight. The segment concludes with a transition to a black and white photograph depicting a person in a white gi lying on their back, seemingly outdoors on rough terrain, with their limbs spread. Japanese text at the bottom left of the photo reads: "口絵２ 浮図" (Kuchi-e 2 Uki-zu - Illustration 2 Floating Figure) and "小田常胤九段「柔道大観」昭和４年" (Oda Tsunetane 9th Dan "Judo Taikan" Showa 4th Year), indicating it's from a 1929 Judo encyclopedia by Oda Tsunetane.

The video displays two black and white photographs of martial arts techniques, set against a blurry, speckled gray background. From 0:00 to 0:23, the first photograph shows two individuals in martial arts gis engaged in a grappling technique. One person, wearing a white gi, is lying on their back, while the other, also in a white gi, is on top, positioned with a knee on the prone person's abdomen. The top person's head is mostly obscured by their gi, while the bottom person's face is visible, looking upwards. Text below the image reads: "口絵2 浮図" (Kuchie 2 Uki-zu - Frontispiece 2: Floating Figure/Technique) and "小田常胤九段「柔道大観」昭和4年" (Oda Tsunetane Kudan "Judo Taikan" Showa 4 Nen - Oda Tsunetane 9th Dan, 'Judo Overview/Compendium,' Showa 4th Year [1929]). At 0:23, the first image transitions to a second black and white photograph, which is displayed until 0:26. This image also features two individuals in martial arts gis demonstrating a technique. One person is lying on their back, and the other is kneeling over them, holding their upper body with both hands in a pinning position. The text below this second image reads: "写真12 浮固" (Shashin 12 Uki-gatame - Photograph 12: Floating Hold/Control) and "有馬純臣四段「有馬柔道教範」大正14年" (Arima Sumio Yodan "Arima Judo Kyohan" Taisho 14 Nen - Arima Sumio 4th Dan, 'Arima Judo Textbook,' Taisho 14th Year [1925]).

The video segment opens with two men in white judogi on a light-colored tatami mat. One man, wearing a white judogi with a red-white belt, is positioned on top of the other man, who is lying on his back wearing a black belt. The top man initially sits on the chest of the man on his back, using his left hand to secure the other's right arm and his right hand to grip the collar near the neck. He then transitions into an "S-mount" position, extending one leg over the opponent's chest and bending the other near the hip, keeping his own buttocks slightly elevated, which signifies the "floating" aspect of the Uki-gatame (浮き固め - "floating hold" or "floating armlock") technique displayed as text in the bottom left corner. During this sequence, the logos for "KODOKAN" (講道館) and "IJF ACADEMY" are visible in the top left and top right corners respectively. The video then transitions to a vintage black and white scene, showing a similar Uki-gatame demonstration. In this historical footage, a man in a white judogi stands over another man lying on the ground, applying an armlock by lifting the opponent's arm, while several other people in judogi are kneeling in the background, observing the technique.

In this black-and-white video segment, two individuals in white judogi are actively engaged in a judo demonstration on a mat in the center of the frame. One individual, likely the 'tori' (thrower), appears to be wearing a dark belt (possibly black due to the monochrome), while the other, the 'uke' (receiver of the throw), has a lighter or unseen belt. They grip each other's uniforms, and the tori executes a powerful throw, sending the uke to the mat with a controlled fall. After the first throw, both individuals quickly recover and stand up, immediately re-engaging to demonstrate another throw, which is performed similarly, resulting in the uke being thrown to the ground once more. In the background, four other men, also dressed in white judogi, are seated in seiza (kneeling position), observing the demonstration attentively. The setting appears to be a dojo with a dark background, suggesting a focused training environment.
